title: Almond amaretto cake
subtitle: Italian-style amaretto-soaked ground almond cake
excerpt: Almond amaretto cake is a dense, moist Italian-style cake made almost entirely from ground almonds, with amaretto soaked in while it's still warm. It's naturally gluten-free, intensely nutty, and the amaretto soak gives it a characteristic marzipan-bitter-almond note. It needs nothing beyond a dusting of icing sugar, though a spoonful of crème fraîche alongside is a good move.
sourceNotes: Ground almond cakes soaked in almond liqueur are well established in northern Italian baking, particularly in Piedmont and Lombardy, where almonds are widely grown and amaretto is produced. The closest Italian archetype is torta di mandorle, which uses ground almonds and eggs with minimal flour. The amaretto soak step is a home adaptation borrowed from the tradition of soaking Italian sponge cakes (pan di spagna) in liqueur, typically Alchermes for trifle-style desserts or rum for tiramisu. In this version the soak is done while the cake is warm so the liqueur penetrates the dense crumb fully rather than pooling on the surface.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze well wrapped before soaking for up to 2 months. Soak with amaretto after defrosting.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before; the amaretto soak intensifies over 24 hours.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional 170°C or fan 150°C; the cake is done when it is golden and pulls away slightly from the tin sides

content.text: Almond amaretto cake is a naturally gluten-free dense cake that smells strongly of marzipan and almond liqueur. The texture is moist and slightly fudgy; a ground almond crumb rather than a sponge. The amaretto soak is done warm, wait too long after the cake comes out of the oven and the soak pools rather than penetrates.

Preheat the oven to 170°C conventional (150°C fan). Grease and line a 22 cm round cake tin with parchment. Combine the ground almonds, caster sugar, and baking powder in a large bowl. In a separate jug, whisk together the eggs, melted butter, and almond extract. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and mix until smooth. Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 35 to 40 minutes. The cake is done when it has pulled away from the sides of the tin and a skewer in the centre comes out with a moist but not wet crumb.

Remove the cake from the oven and immediately prick the surface all over with a skewer, going deep into the cake. Pour the amaretto evenly over the surface. It will foam slightly where it meets the hot cake. Leave the cake to cool completely in the tin, the soak will be absorbed as it cools. Once cool, remove from the tin and dust lightly with icing sugar to serve.
